newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Trade gap mars Vietnam's rosy growth picture.
newsitem.headline: Trade gap mars Vietnam's rosy growth picture.

text.p: Industrial output growth quickened in Vietnam this month, but its booming economy continued to suck in imports faster than it could sell goods abroad, official figures showed on Monday.
The Statistics Department estimated that industrial production was 13.9 percent higher in February than in the same month of 1996, up from January's growth rate of 12.9 percent.
Output from the state sector, which dominates the communist country's economy, rose by a year-on-year 12.6 percent while the burgeoning foreign-invested sector saw growth of 22.5 percent.
Vietnam's economic growth, generated by government reforms along market lines, has topped eight percent since 1992.
However, a growing appetite for imports left it with a record trade deficit of $4.0 billion in 1996 -- equivalent to some 18 percent of annual national income.

The statistics office, which often estimates monthly economic indicators before the month has ended, said the trade gap narrowed to $223 million in February from $420 million in January. But the total deficit for the first two months of the year -- $643 million -- was up 11 percent from the same period of 1996.
